content.summary: Reviewed the substantive code before integration acceptance. Generated proposals now enter actual search, reconstruction and Java comparison, but cannot resolve their own source meaning. The upcoming phase tests persistence, authority and source-first annotations together with the previous workbench.
findings: P1 validated all-unit disposition, six interpretation dimensions, exact unique quote references, context isolation, and shared allowance race behavior.
P2 tests compare generated classes and replay an SMT witness at an inclusive threshold, retain differing fact bindings, and reject vacuous stable-extension acceptance.
P3 exercised generated children, BFS and UCT selection, backpropagation, isolated roundtrip requests, universal omission, encoding failure, interrupted dispatch and report omission.
Reviewed canonical serialization: floating point settings and nanosecond integers exceeded project canonical constraints; changed to integer milli-units and string timestamps before acceptance.
Candidate storage and release binding commit in the same transaction. Uncompiled readings survive as unresolved candidates.
Legal approval is not synthesized: annotation identities and attestation are local prototype controls; actual independent human corpus remains absent.
Live pilot acceptance requires three source-driven initial outputs, new children and an actual reconstruction response. A terminal blocked report alone cannot pass it.
Provider error handling and unknown-result recovery are bounded. CLI-internal transport behavior remains an external assumption and is disclosed rather than claimed as exact model-request accounting.
